newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Stet must pay state 120 bln lire.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Stet must pay state 120 bln lire.

text.p: Italian telecommunications holding Stet must pay the state 120 billion lire ($74.9 million) as part of a complex balancing act involving Italy's two mobile phone operators, Post and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said on Thursday.

As a result of this payment, Italy's second mobile phone company, Omnitel, will not now receive 60 billion lire in reimbursements from Stet's operating units, Maccanico told a parliamentary commission.

Omnitel, an international consortium controlled by Olivetti, launched its GSM mobile phone service in December 1995 to compete with Stet's cellular phone division, now grouped in its unit Telecom Italia Mobile.
Omnitel was forced to pay the state a 750 billion lire licence fee to enter the cellular market.
It complained to the European Union, arguing that Stet did not have to pay anything when it started its mobile phone business.

The European Commission backed Omnitel and agreed with the government in late 1995 that the second mobile phone operator should receive reductions in connection fees to state-controlled telephone lines worth some 60 billion lire.
European Commissioner Karel Van Miert wrote to Maccanico this week to complain that the legislation opening the way for the reduction had still not been put in place.
Maccanico told parliament on Thursday that the alternative solution had been to ask Stet to hand over to the state 120 billion lire to partly balance the Omnitel licence fee.
With the connection fee legislation blocked, he said this second option had now come into force.
"I don't know if (Stet) has already paid up, but it will have to," he said.
